split.policy: dev cases may be used to develop and tune the harness. held-out cases are frozen and excluded from the development loop, reserved for final reporting. Both are published because all pilot v1 cases are synthetic (PRIV-08).
split.note: Immutable regression core never changes; refresh rotates the remaining cases.

providers.name: Hermes built-in memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md)
providers.notes: Always active alongside any external provider; restart-safe (state on disk, re-injected at session start). Observed active in dev environment (provider audit t_8728060f).

providers.name: Hermes session_search (FTS5 over SQLite state DB)
providers.notes: Retrieval baseline over past sessions; state.db present in dev environment. Needs populated session DB for meaningful retrieval.

providers.name: Lexical/BM25 retrieval baseline (harness reference)
providers.notes: Not a provider. Runner-implemented deterministic baseline (recommended: SQLite FTS5/BM25 over synthetic event text, fixed top_k). Never promoted to a provider measurement.

providers.name: No-memory base model reference
providers.notes: Base-model reference with no provider; measures model-only behavior. Current default state of the dev environment (provider audit §1).

providers.name: Hindsight (Vectorize)
providers.notes: Plugin ships bundled in v0.20.0 (cloud mode default, or local_external daemon). Not configured in dev environment; requires HINDSIGHT_API_KEY (cloud) or a running daemon at http://localhost:8888 plus an LLM provider key (local).
setup_failures: not-configured: no local hindsight daemon endpoint available

providers.name: Mnemosyne (mnemosyne-oss)
providers.notes: NOT bundled in v0.20.0 (absent from provider list; vendor 'ships enabled' claim not observed). Requires user install (mnemosyne-hermes + memory profile) and an embedding endpoint or ~800 MB RAM for local embeddings. MCP path (mnemosyne mcp) is an alternative.
setup_failures: not-configured: no MNEMOSYNE_EMBEDDING_API_KEY / OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY supplied

claim_evidence_classes.definition: Measured by this benchmark in a controlled run.

integration_states.definition: Ships with the named Hermes release and is active without extra setup.
Installed as a third-party plugin; may require credentials or a daemon.
Reachable only through MCP; not a native memory provider.
Integrated via hooks rather than the memory provider interface.
Documented by the vendor but not observed working in this environment.
Tested against a named Hermes release by this project.
Present or documented but not configured; never scored as measured.

privacy_rules.rule: Synthetic content only. All scenario fixtures use invented entities, hosts, projects, values, and conversations. No real persons, addresses, credentials, file paths, hostnames, or machine identifiers.

No real conversation material. Nothing from actual Hermes sessions may be copied into fixtures or reports. Real-world interaction shapes may inspire scenarios; content is rewritten with invented names and facts.

No documents, binaries, or extracted text. PDFs, DOCX files, archives, and extracted plain text from memorypapers/ (or anywhere else) must never be committed. Public documentation cites stable DOI, arXiv, or publisher URLs only.
Private seeds stay private. Committed fixtures and manifests contain public seeds only; private seeds are referenced by pointer and never by value.
Credentials are synthetic and flagged. Any invented credential-like value is clearly fictional, prefixed to be obviously synthetic (e.g. hlab-...), and marked privacy.contains_credentials: true.
Redacted configs. Run manifests record provider.config_redacted as a human-readable summary with secrets removed. Raw configs, tokens, and keys never appear in committed artifacts.
Raw logs stay local. Raw provider dumps and conversation logs referenced by results (provenance.raw_log_uri) are local-only, never committed.
Held-out cases are frozen but public. Pilot v1 held-out scenarios are synthetic and published; held-out means excluded from the development/tuning loop, not hidden.
Licensed adaptation requires citation. Any scenario adapted from a public benchmark cites the stable source (origin.source_ref) and declares its license; local copies of the source are not committed.
Scan before commit. Every fixture, manifest, and result must pass the public-safety substring scan in tools/validate_fixtures.py before it is committed or published.
